context: A profile's lenses list is the complete ordered set for a run and replaces the default lens set rather than adding to it. This scenario checks that adopting one lens keeps the four defaults running, that the refs are pinned, and that the profile is checked rather than assumed.

checklist.name: Profile written at the discovered path
checklist.description: A block-style YAML profile exists at the repository root as .tessl-code-review.yml with schemaVersion: 1 and a non-empty lenses list

checklist.name: Defaults kept
checklist.description: The lenses list names all four default lenses (review-correctness-and-data-integrity, review-maintainability-and-code-quality, review-scale-and-resilience, review-security-and-privacy) as well as the local lens ./review-lenses/review-per-row-calls/SKILL.md

checklist.name: States why the defaults had to be listed
checklist.description: plan.md says that a profile's lens list is the complete set for the run and replaces the defaults rather than adding to them, so a profile naming only the new lens would silently stop running the others

checklist.name: Registry refs are pinned
checklist.description: Every registry ref in the profile carries an explicit version, such as tessl/code-review@0.4.0#review-security-and-privacy, and none is left unpinned

checklist.name: No unrequested policy change
checklist.description: The profile does not set model, supervisorModel, or supervisorEffort, and plan.md does not propose changing when reviews run or whether they block

checklist.name: Checked before being handed over
checklist.description: plan.md tells the team to run tessl code review check-profile, spelled exactly that way, before merging, and says that a lens selecting zero files is a defect to fix rather than a warning to note
